newsitem.title: USA: US Northwest spot prods ease with NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: US Northwest spot prods ease with NYMEX.

text.p: U.S. Northwest product prices eased on Thursday, reacting to weaker futures on NYMEX and the return of a major regional pipeline.
Olympic Pipeline, which carries around 325,000 barrels-per-day of refined products through Washington state and Oregon, underwent a day of repairs which ended on Thursday.
Supply was affected in Portland rather than Seattle, traders said.
The region's refineries were trouble-free, traders said, adding further pressure after the pipeline's return.
Regular unleaded gasoline was assessed at 69.00 cents to 70.00 cents a gallon, off about two cents from Wednesday.
Premium was seen 7.50 cents a gallon higher.
In distillates, jet fuel fell one cent to 79/80 cents a gallon and low sulphur diesel eased two to three cents, with cargoes due up from California suppliers.
